tier_reason: Peer-reviewed IEEE IoT Journal 2025 paper exists (DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2025.3541247 cited in README), but the paper, ieeexplore and the press release (eurekalert) are egress-blocked; the 53%/23% figures were seen only in search snippets of the press release and CNX Software. Repo has no benchmark code or numbers, so the win could not be checked against the paper; capped at C until the paper is read.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Up to 53% faster execution time and 23% lower memory usage than glibc ptmalloc; 530 lines of code and 20 KB vs ptmalloc's 4838 lines and 116 KB (press release and CNX Software snippets only; paper not opened).
corrections.caveats: Numbers from press-release search snippets only; paper (IEEE IoT Journal 2025) blocked here and repo README carries no numbers or benchmark code (only lwmalloc.c, Makefile, test.c). No LICENSE file in the repo (LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING all 404), so reference only. Compares to ptmalloc, not jemalloc or mimalloc; targets single-board embedded systems (Raspberry Pi Zero W, Pi 4, Jetson Orin Nano).

notes: Real peer-reviewed allocator; retier to B if the IEEE paper becomes reachable and shows the ptmalloc comparison. Stars 93, 10 commits, last commit 2026-07-07 confirmed on github.com.

tier_reason: PLDI 2019 paper checked into the repo states every claimed number (Firefox -16% vs bundled jemalloc, Redis -39%, perlbench peak RSS 564 MB vs 664/614/732 MB, SPECint geomean memory -2.4% and runtime +0.7%, perlbench +3.9%) plus clang 4.0 -O2 / gcc 8 -O3 -flto on an i7-5600U. Peer-reviewed but no dedicated benchmark harness in the repo, so B not A.
notes: Win is memory footprint, not speed (runtime equal or slightly worse); metric 'memory' is correctly set. Apache-2.0, 1.9k stars, last commit 2026-03-25 verified.

tier_reason: ISMM 2020 peer-reviewed paper (PDF blocked; claim seen in search snippet), and the repo's own result CSVs under data/{threadtest,shbench,larson}/ with the benchmark code in test/ corroborate it: threadtest 28.7 s vs Makalu 298 s and PMDK 1690 s at 1 thread, Larson 4.8e8 vs Makalu 1.27e7 ops at 88 threads (about 37x, derived from page data). Compiler flags and CPU model not seen, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: ISMM 2020 paper (search snippet): about 10x faster than Makalu and PMDK on Threadtest and Shbench, up to 37x faster than Makalu on Larson. Repo CSVs (derived from page data): Threadtest 1 thread 28.7 s vs Makalu 298 s, PMDK 1690 s, jemalloc 38.4 s; 40 threads 2.31 s vs Makalu 52.2 s, PMDK 118 s; Larson 88 threads 4.8e8 ops vs Makalu 1.27e7, PMDK 6.46e6, jemalloc 5.2e8.
corrections.caveats: Baselines are persistent-memory allocators (Makalu, PMDK libpmemobj); against transient jemalloc it is roughly on par at low thread counts and 2-3x slower on Threadtest and Shbench above 48 threads (repo CSVs). Paper PDF blocked here; claim cross-checked against repo data/*.csv only. Bundled LRMalloc hazard counter can overflow above ~72 threads (README warning). Last commit 2020-10-23.

notes: MIT LICENSE confirmed; 48 stars, 13 forks, last commit 2020-10-23 (abandoned). Repo data independently supports the paper's ratios.
